patch.value: Work economics: the tracker decides what is worth doing by comparing measured cost against forecast value, instead of ranking on urgency alone

Every input to an economic decision is either shipped or filed, and nothing consumes them. Token accounting reports what an invocation cost (pm-t5dt4z). Fleet analytics derive per-harness and per-model throughput, rework and defect-escape rates (pm-gw6uyq). Probabilistic forecasting estimates delivery distributions over the dependency graph (pm-uey8od). Fleet allocation assigns capability-matched work along the critical path (pm-3oqjnc). What no item owns is the objective function these feed: a comparison of the expected cost of doing a piece of work against the expected value of having done it, so that a fleet with more capacity than backlog can decline low-value work rather than execute the whole queue because the queue exists. The absence shows up as a specific failure mode at scale — an autonomous fleet maximises throughput because throughput is the only thing it can measure, and a tracker holding decades of outcomes can measure whether the work mattered. The value side is derivable from data the tracker already holds: which items were later reopened, superseded, cancelled, or closed as duplicate; which produced learnings that were subsequently retrieved; which unblocked how much downstream work; which released capacity on the critical path. This item owns that objective function and nothing else — it does not schedule, does not measure cost, and does not forecast.

Expected value derives only from recorded outcomes already in the tracker — reopen, supersede, cancel, duplicate, downstream unblocking, learning retrieval — never from a hand-assigned score; Expected cost derives from measured invocation and throughput data rather than from estimates, with estimates used only where no measurement exists and labelled as such; Every ranking decision reports its cost term, its value term, and the evidence behind each, so a human can disagree with a specific number rather than with an opaque order; The model is calibrated against history: a backtest shows whether items it would have declined were in fact later reopened, superseded or cancelled; Declining work is a recorded decision with a rationale and a revisit condition, never a silent omission from a queue; A workspace with no outcome history degenerates exactly to today's priority and critical-path ordering with no new configuration; The value model is replaceable through the SDK so a domain can supply its own without forking the scheduler
Give a fleet an economic reason to not do work, derived from its own recorded outcomes
Capacity goes to work that measurably mattered, and low-value work is declined with a recorded rationale instead of executed by default
Changes the fleet objective from throughput to realised value, which is the difference between an autonomous tracker that compounds and one that churns
A declared, inspectable value model with calibration against recorded outcomes, consumed by allocation and reported per decision
Cost measurement, outcome analytics, forecasting and allocation are each filed or shipped, so the objective function is now the only missing link in the chain
